HWM and LHX. Howmet Aerospace and L3Harris.

His accounts picked up over $200,000 of each in 2025, part of a defense buying wave totaling at least $10 million that year.

Howmet makes jet engine components. L3Harris does defense electronics and surveillance tech.

Both sit right inside his defense priorities.

He has pushed for military budgets as high as $1.5 trillion. His administration wants stockpiles rebuilt and AI integrated into military systems.

These two companies live in the supply chain for exactly that hardware.

Then came the Iran escalations.

Military aircraft and surveillance systems saw heavy use. The Pentagon replaced and upgraded what got expended.

Every part replaced, every system upgraded, flows through companies like these two.

The giant contractors grab the headlines. These are the quieter picks.

That is becoming the pattern in this portfolio. The big names everyone knows, plus the smaller, more exotic ones nobody is watching.

Both types moved with the defense wave as the contracts flowed.

As always, the White House says independent managers handle everything with no input from him.

The pattern doesn’t change either way. The administration drives the spending. The portfolio owns the supply chain.

We will keep reading every disclosure.
